41:1: Abu Ja`far said: We have already stated before what we have said about the meaning of <Ha Mim>, and the statement on this topic is like the statement on that.
41:2: And His statement: A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. God Almighty says: This Qur’an is a revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. He sent it down to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
41:3: A Book whose verses are explained in detail. He says: A Book whose verses are explained in detail. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement: His verses are detailed, he said: His verses are made clear. And His saying: An Arabic Qur’an, God Almighty says: Its verses are explained in detail in this way. Arabic grammarians differed about the reason for the accusative case of the Qur’an. Some of the grammarians of Basra said that his statement, A Book detailed means the Book is the predicate of a subject that states that the revelation is a Book. Then he said, Its verses were detailed, an Arabic Qur’an, making the verb preoccupied with the verses until it became like the subject, so he put the Qur’an in the accusative case. He said, A bearer of good tidings and a warner, as an adjective. If you wish, you can make it accusative for praise, as if when he mentioned it, he began to praise it, so he said, We mentioned an Arabic Qur’an, a bearer of good tidings and a warner, and We mentioned it as an Arabic Qur’an. What preceded in mentioning it was evidence of what was implied. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said, He put the Qur’an in the accusative case as a verb, meaning its verses were detailed in this way. He said, The accusative case may be for severance, because the speech is complete when he said, ‘His verses.’ He said: If it had been raised as an attribute of the Book, it would have been correct, as he said in another place: A blessed Book which We have revealed to you [p. 29]. And he said: Likewise, his saying: A bearer of good tidings and a warner contains what is in an Arabic Qur’an. And His statement: For a people who know means: The verses of this Book were explained in detail as an Arabic Qur’an for a people who know the Arabic language, bringing them good tidings, giving them good tidings if they believe in it and act according to what was revealed in it of God’s limits and obligations, of Paradise. And as a warner: He says: And a warner of whoever denies it and does not act according to what is in it, of God’s command in this worldly life and of eternal damnation in the fire of Hell in the Hereafter. And His statement: But most of them turned away means that God Almighty says: So they were too arrogant to listen to it and ponder the proofs of God in it, and most of these people to whom this Qur’an was sent down as a bearer of good tidings and a warner turned away from it, and they are the people of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So they do not listen means that they do not listen to it or hear it, out of turning away from it and being arrogant.
41:4: As a bringer of good tidings and a warner, but most of them turned away and did not hear.
41:5: God the Almighty says: “And these polytheists who turned away from the signs of God, from the polytheists of Quraysh, said when Muhammad, the Prophet of God, called them to acknowledge the Oneness of God and to believe in what is in this Quran of God’s commands and prohibitions, and all that was revealed therein, “Our hearts are within coverings” meaning: in coverings from that which you call to O Muhammad “of the Oneness of God and your belief in what you have brought to us. We do not understand what you say. “And in our ears is deafness” meaning heaviness, we do not hear what you call to out of the weight and aversion to what he calls to.” The meanings of these letters were explained before with their supporting evidence, and what the people of interpretation said about them was mentioned, so we disliked repeating that in this place. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Our hearts are within coverings, he said: They have coverings on them like quivers for arrows. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And they said, ‘Our hearts are within coverings,’ he said: coverings over them, and in our ears is deafness, he said: deafness. And His saying: And between us and you is a veil. They say: And between us and you, O Muhammad, is a veil because of which we and you cannot meet, and we cannot see each other. And that veil is their difference in religion, because their religion was the worship of idols, and the religion of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him. And that is the veil that they claimed was between them and the Prophet of God, and that is their disagreement with each other in religion. And his saying: Then work, for we will work. He says: They said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Then work, O Muhammad, according to your religion and what you say is the truth. We will work according to our religion and what we say is the truth. And leave our call to what you call us to of your religion, for we will call your call to our religion.” The word min was inserted in his statement: And between us and you is a veil, meaning: And between us and you is a veil, to emphasize the statement.
41:6: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those of your people who turn away from the signs of God: O people, I am only a human being from the children of Adam, like you in kind, form and appearance. I am not an angel. It is revealed to me means: God reveals to me that you have no deity worthy of worship except One deity. So be upright towards Him means: So be upright towards Him in obedience, and direct your faces towards Him in desire and worship, not towards gods and idols. And seek His forgiveness means: And ask Him to pardon you for your past sins by repenting from your polytheism, and He will accept your repentance and forgive you.
41:7: And His statement: And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat and who, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers. God Almighty says: And the pus of the people of Hell, and what flows from them, for those who claim to have a partner with God, worshipping idols instead of Him, who do not give zakat. The commentators differed on this. Some of them said: Its meaning is: those who do not give God the obedience that purifies them and sanctifies their bodies, and do not believe in His Oneness. This is a statement attributed to Ibn Abbas. The narration mentioned that: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat, he said: They are those who do not testify that there is no god but God. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me, he said: Hafs told us, he said: Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, his statement: And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat means those who do not say there is no god but God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: those who do not acknowledge the zakat on their money that God has imposed on it, and do not give it to its people. We have also mentioned those who said this before. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And woe to the polytheists * Who do not give zakat. He said: They do not acknowledge it nor believe in it. It was said: Zakat is the bridge to Islam, whoever cuts it off will be saved, and whoever refrains from it will perish. The apostates after the Prophet of God said: As for the prayer, we pray, and as for the zakat, by God, do not seize our wealth. Abu Bakr said: By God, I do not separate between something that God has joined together, and by God, if they withhold from me even a rope from what God and His Messenger have enjoined, I will fight them over it. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And woe to the polytheists * who do not give zakat. He said: If they paid zakat while they were polytheists, it would not benefit them. The correct statement about this is what was said by those who said: Its meaning is: They do not pay zakat on their wealth. This is because this is the most well-known meaning of zakat, and His statement, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, is evidence that this is the case, because the disbelievers meant by this verse did not testify that there is no god but God. If His statement, those who do not pay zakat, meant those who do not testify that there is no god but God, His statement, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, would not have had any meaning, because it is known that whoever does not testify that there is no god but God does not believe in the Hereafter. In following God’s statement, and they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, His statement, those who do not pay zakat, indicates that zakat in this context refers to zakat on wealth. His statement: And they are disbelievers in the Hereafter, meaning: And they are disbelievers in the establishment of the Hour, and God will raise His creation alive from their graves after their affliction and destruction.
41:8: God Almighty says: “Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and did what God and His Messenger commanded them to do, and refrained from what We forbade them from - and that is the righteous deeds - will have a reward uninterrupted.” He says: For those who do that, there will be a reward undiminished from what He promised them to reward them for. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and we have explained it previously in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: For them is a reward uninterrupted. Some of them said: Undiminished. Some of them said: Uninterrupted. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: An unfailing reward means: undiminished. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: For them is a reward uninterrupted, he said: It is calculated.
41:9: And His saying: Indeed, you disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days, that is, Sunday and Monday. And this is what the reports came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the scholars said. We have mentioned much of this before, and we will mention some of what we did not mention before, God willing. He mentioned some of the report that we did not mention before: Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Saeed al-Baqqal, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas - Hannad said: I read the rest of the hadith to Abu Bakr - “The Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and asked him about the creation of the heavens and the earth. He said: God created the earth on Sunday and Monday, and created the mountains on Tuesday and all the benefits in them, and created on Wednesday the trees, water, cities, built-up areas, and ruins. So these are four. Then he said: Do you disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and make rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed therein firm mountains above it and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, equal for those who ask, for whoever asks. He said: And on Thursday He created the heaven, and on Friday He created the stars, the sun, the moon, and the angels, until three hours remained of it. In the first of these three hours He created the appointed time when whoever dies, and in the second He cast afflictions on everything that benefits people, and in the third He created Adam and settled him in Paradise, and He ordered Iblis to prostrate to him, and He expelled him from it in the last hour.” The Jews said, Then what then, O Muhammad? He said, Then He established Himself on the Throne. They said, You would have been right if you had completed it. They said, Then He rested. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, became extremely angry, so the verse was revealed, “And We created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us. So be patient over what they say.” (Qaf: 38) Tamim bin Al-Muntasir narrated to us: Ishaq informed us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ghalib bin Ghallab, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God created one day and named it Sunday. Then He created a second and named it Monday. Then He created a third and named it Tuesday. Then He created a fourth and named it Wednesday. Then He created a fifth and named it Thursday. He said: So He created the earth in two days, Sunday and Monday, and He created the mountains on Tuesday, and that is what the people say: It is a heavy day. He created the locations of the rivers and trees on Wednesday, and He created the birds, wild animals, vermin, and beasts on Thursday, and He created man on Friday, so He finished creating everything on Friday. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, He created the earth in two days on Sunday and Monday. And it has been said otherwise. This is what Al-Qasim bin Bishr bin Maruf and Al-Hussein bin Ali told me. They said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ismail bin Umayya told me, on the authority of Ayoub bin Khalid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Rafi’, the freed slave of Umm Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took my hand and said: God created the soil on Saturday, and created the mountains in it on Sunday, and created the trees on Monday, and created the unpleasant things on Tuesday, and created the light on Wednesday, and spread the animals in it on Thursday, and created Adam after the afternoon prayer on Friday, the last creation in the last hour of the hours of Friday, between the afternoon prayer and the night.” His statement: And you attribute to Him rivals, meaning: And you attribute to the One Who created this way rivals, and they are equal men whom you obey in disobeying God. We have already explained the meaning of rivals with evidence previously. And His statement: That is the Lord of the worlds means: He who performed this action and created the earth in two days is the Owner of all the jinn and mankind, and all other kinds of creation, and everything below Him is owned by Him. So how can it be possible for Him to have a rival? And can a powerless slave who is unable to do anything be a rival to his Owner who is able to do it?
41:10: God Almighty says: And He placed on the earth which He created in two days firm mountains, which are the fixed ones on the earth above it, meaning: above the earth on its surface. His saying: And blessed it means: And He blessed the earth and made it always good for its people. It was mentioned on the authority of Al-Saddī in this regard: Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And blessed it he said: He caused its trees to grow. And measured therein its sustenance The interpreters differed on this. Some of them said: He determined therein the sustenance of its people, meaning their provisions and livelihoods. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Hasan: And He has measured therein its sustenance. He said: Its provisions. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement, And measured therein its sustenance, he said: He measured therein the provisions of the servants, the One with sustenance. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And He has measured therein its sustenance, meaning: its sustenance for its people. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: He determined for it what would be suitable for it. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told me, he said: Al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Khalid bin Da’laj, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And He has measured therein its sustenance, he said: its provision. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And He determined therein its mountains, rivers, and trees. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And He determined therein its sustenance: He created therein its mountains, rivers, seas, trees, and all its inhabitants from among the animals. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And He has measured therein its sustenance. He said: Its mountains, its animals, its rivers, and its seas. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that its sustenance was determined from the rain. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And measured therein its sustenance, he said: from the rain. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He determined in each town what He did not make in the other town, due to the livelihood of some of them from others through trade from town to town. Who said that? Al-Husayn bin Muhammad Al-Dhara’ told me, he said: Abu Muhsin told us, he said: Husayn told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement: And measured therein its sustenance, he said: Al-Yamani is in Yemen, and Al-Sabari is in Sabur. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me, he said: Abu Muhsin told us on the authority of Hisin, he said: Ikrimah said, And He measured therein its sustenance, the Yamaniyyah in Yemen, and the Sabiriyah in Sabur, and similar things. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Hisin on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And He has measured therein its sustenance, he said: In every land there is sustenance that is not suitable in any other land, the Yemeni in Yemen, and the Sabari in Sabur. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Husayn told us on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: And He has measured therein its sustenance, he said: The land in which there is sustenance or something that is not for anyone else, do you not see that the sabari is only in Sabur, and the asab is only in Yemen and so on. Ismail bin Saif told me, he said: Ibn Abd al-Wahid bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And measured therein its sustenance, he said: Al-Sabari is in Sabur, and Al-Tayalisah is from Rayy. Ismail told me, he said: Abu Al-Nadr, the companion of Al-Basri, told us, he said: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, regarding his statement: And measured therein its sustenance, he said: Al-Sabari is from Sabur, and Al-Tayalisah is from Rayy. The correct statement about this is to say: God Almighty has informed us that He has determined on the earth the sustenance of its people, and that is what sustains them of food and provides them with a livelihood. He, the Most High, did not specify in His statement, And has determined therein its sustenance, that He has determined therein one sustenance rather than another. Rather, He made the statement general about His determining therein all sustenance, and that which sustains its people is that which nothing else provides them with of food, and that does not happen except through rain and the management of the lands, as He has specified some with it and not others, and from what He has brought forth from the mountains of jewels, and from the sea of food and ornaments. I do not say anything more correct about that than what He, the Most High, said: He has determined on the earth the sustenance of its people, for the reason we have described. And He, the Most High, said: In four days, based on what we mentioned before from the report that we narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, “On the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he completed the creation of the earth and all of its causes and benefits, from trees, water, cities, civilizations, and ruins, in four days, the first of which was Sunday, and the last of which was Wednesday.” Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: He created the mountains in it, the sustenance of its people, its trees, and what is appropriate for it in two days, Tuesday and Wednesday. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said: He created the earth in two days, then he said in four days, because he means that this and the first are four days, just as you say: I married a woman yesterday, and today two, and one of them is the one I married yesterday. And His statement: It is equal for those who ask. The people of interpretation differed in its interpretation. Some of them said: Its interpretation is: It is equal for whoever asks about the amount of the term in which God created the earth, and placed in it the firm mountains above it and the blessing, and measured in it the sustenance for its people, and he finds it as God has informed, four days, neither more nor less than that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It is the same for those who ask. Whoever asks about that will find it, as God said. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: It is the same for those who ask. He said: Whoever asks, it is as God said. Musa bin Harun told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: In four days, equal for those who ask. He said: Whoever asks, this is how it is. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: It is the same for whoever asks his Lord for something he needs in terms of sustenance, for God has already determined for him sustenance on earth, according to the amount of each questioner’s request. If he had asked Him, His knowledge of them would not have been exhausted before He created them. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: It is the same for those who ask, he said: He measured that according to the amount of their questions, and he knows that they will not be anything of their questions except something that He knew before it came to be. The reciters differed in their recitation of this word. The majority of reciters in the regions, except for Abu Ja`far and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, recited it as sawa`an in the accusative case. Abu Ja`far, the reciter, recited it as sawa`an in the nominative case. Al-Hasan recited sawa`an in the genitive case. The correct reading of this is what the reciters of the regions have done, which is to read it in the accusative case, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on this, and because its meaning is correct. That is because the meaning of the statement is: And He has measured therein its sustenance equally for those who ask for it, according to their need and according to what is good for them. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Masoud that he used to recite: And He divided therein its sustenance. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative case of sawa’an. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: Whoever puts it in the accusative case makes it a verbal noun, as if he said: istawa’an. He said: It has also been read in the genitive case and made a noun for the levels: that is, in four complete days. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Whoever puts sawa’an in the genitive case makes it an adjective for the days, or if you like, an adjective for the four, and whoever puts it in the accusative case makes it connected to the provisions. He said: It has also been raised as if it were a subject, as if he said: That is sawa’an for the questioners, meaning: for whoever wants to know it. The correct statement about this is that it is in the accusative case when it is in the accusative case as a state of sustenance, if it is equal and is likened to indefinite nouns, so it is said: I passed by equal people, so it follows indefinite nouns. And if it follows indefinite nouns, it is cut off from definite nouns and is in the accusative case, so it is said: I passed by your brothers equally. It is also permissible that if it does not have a dual or plural, it is likened to masdars. As for if it is in the nominative case, it is in the nominative case starting with the pronoun of that and the like. And if it is in the genitive case, it follows the days or the four.
41:11: And His statement: Then He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion.’ They said, ‘We come willingly.’ Meaning, the Most High, mentioned: Then He directed Himself to the heaven, then ascended to the heaven. We have already explained the statements of the scholars on this matter previously. And His saying: And He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion,’ God Almighty says: God said to the heaven and the earth, “Bring what I have created in you. As for you, O heaven, bring forth what I have created in you of the sun, the moon, and the stars. As for you, O earth, bring forth what I have created in you of trees, fruits, and plants, and split open the rivers.” They said, We have come willingly, “We have come with what You have created in us of Your creation, and responding to Your command, we do not disobey Your command.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Abu Hisham told us: Ibn Yaman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then He said to it and to the earth, ‘Come, willingly or by compulsion.’ They said, ‘We come willingly.’ He said: God said to the heavens: ‘Bring forth My sun and moon, and bring forth My stars.’ And He said to the earth: ‘Spread forth your rivers and bring forth your fruits.’ They said: ‘Give us willingly.’” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman al-Ahwal, on the authority of Tawus, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, Bring: give. And regarding His statement, They said, ‘We have come’: they said, ‘We have given.’ And it was said: We came willingly, and He did not say obediently. The heaven and the earth are feminine, because the nun and the alif that are a metaphor for their names in His statement, We have come are similar to the metaphor for the names of the male informants about themselves, so He made His statement, obediently, follow the same pattern as the information about men. Some of the Arab scholars used to say: He took him to the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them. Others among them said: It was said thus because when they spoke, they resembled the males of the sons of Adam.
41:12: God Almighty says: He completed the creation of seven heavens in two days, which were Thursday and Friday. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: He directed Himself to the heaven while it was smoke from the breathing of water when it breathed, and He made it one heaven, then He split it apart, and He made them seven heavens in two days, Thursday and Friday. And it was called Friday because on it He gathered together the creation of the heavens and the earth. His saying: And He revealed to each heaven its command, meaning: And He cast into each of the seven heavens what He wanted of creation. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And He revealed to each heaven its command, he said: What God commanded and willed. Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And He revealed in each heaven its command. He said: He created in each heaven its creation of angels and the creation in it of seas and mountains of hail, and what is not known. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And He revealed in each heaven its command, meaning He created something in it, its sun, its moon, its stars, and its goodness. And His statement: And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as protection. God Almighty says: And We have adorned the lowest heaven for you, O people, with the stars, which are the lamps. As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps. He said: Then He adorned the heaven with stars, making them an adornment and a protection from the devils. The Arabists differed about the reason for placing the word in the accusative case in his statement: and preservation. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is in the accusative case in the sense of: And We preserved it with preservation, as if he had said: And We preserve it with preservation, because when he said: We adorned it with lamps, he had informed that he had looked into its matter and looked after it, so this indicates preservation, as if he had said: And We preserved it with preservation. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is in the accusative case in the sense of: And We adorned it with preservation, because if the waw had been dropped, it would have been: Indeed, We adorned the lowest heaven with preservation. This second statement is closer to the truth in our view than the first. We have explained the reason for this in a similar place in more than one place in this book, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement: That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing, God Almighty says: This that I have described to you of My creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them, and My adornment of the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars, as I have explained, is the decree of the Almighty in His punishment of His enemies, the All-Knowing of the secrets and open secrets of His servants, and their management according to what is best for them.
41:13: God Almighty says: If these polytheists turn away from this argument that you, O Muhammad, explain to them, and you alert them to it, and they do not believe in it and do not acknowledge that the one who does that is God, besides whom there is no god, then say to them: I have warned you, O people, of a thunderbolt that will destroy you like the thunderbolt of Aad and Thamud. We have previously explained that the meaning of thunderbolt is: everything that spoils something and changes its state. It has been said in this context that it refers to a calamity and punishment from God. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: A thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Aad and Thamud, he said: He says: I have warned you of a calamity like the calamity of ‘Aad and Thamud. He said: A punishment like the punishment of ‘Aad and Thamud.
41:14: And His statement: When there came to them the messengers from before them and from behind them means: Say: I have warned you of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud that destroyed them, when the messengers came to 'Ad and Thamud from before them, so His statement: <when>is a connection to thunderbolt. And what He meant by His statement: from before them are the messengers that came to the fathers of those who were destroyed by the thunderbolt from these two nations. And what He meant by His statement: and from behind them is from behind the messengers who were sent to their fathers as messengers to them. That is because God sent Hud to 'Ad, but they denied him after messengers who had preceded him to their fathers as well, so they denied them, and so they were destroyed. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: If they turn away... to his statement: and those behind them, he said: The messengers who were before Hud, and the messengers who were after him. God sent messengers before him, and sent messengers after him. And His statement: That you worship none but God means, the Most High said: The messengers came to them with the order that they should worship none but God alone, with no partner for Him. They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down angels means, the Most High said: So they said to their messengers when they called them to acknowledge the oneness of God: If our Lord had willed that we worship Him alone and not worship anything besides Him, He would have sent down to us angels from the heaven as messengers with what you call us to. He would not have sent you, even though you are human beings like us, but He was pleased with our worshipping what we worship, and for that reason He did not send angels to us to forbid us from that. And His statement: Then we are disbelievers in that with which you have been sent. He says: They said to their messengers: Then we are disbelievers in that with which your Lord has sent you to us, not believing in it.
41:15: God Almighty says: “As for ‘Aad, the people of Hud, they were arrogant towards their Lord and acted tyrannically in the land, arrogantly and insolently, without permission from God, and they said, ‘Who is stronger than us in strength?’ Did they not see that God, who created them and gave them what He gave them of great creation and great power, was stronger than them in strength, so they would fear His punishment and guard against His wrath, because of their disbelief in Him and their denial of His messengers. And they used to deny Our signs.” He says: And they used to deny Our proofs and arguments against them.
41:16: God Almighty says: Then We sent upon the people of Aad a furious wind. The commentators differed on the meaning of as-sarar. Some of them said: It means a strong wind. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: A violent wind he said: Strong. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A violent wind, very poisonous for them. Others said: Rather, he meant that it was cold. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, So We sent upon them a furious wind. He said: The furious wind is the cold. Ibn Abi Al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: a furious wind, he said: cold. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, A furious wind. He said: A cold, loud wind. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say, regarding His statement: a furious wind, he said: a wind with intense cold. The more correct of the two sayings is the saying of Mujahid, and that is that his saying: Sarraran is only the sound of the wind when it blows violently, so it is heard like the saying of the one who says: Sarraar. Then he made that because of the doubling in the ra, so he said: Then one of the ras was replaced with a sad because of the abundance of ra, as it was said in raddahu: radraddahu, and in nahhahu: nahana, as Ru’bah said: Today I have come to my senses, and my first dream is not a disaster. As he said in his palm: his palm, as Al-Nabigha said: I hold back a tear that has overcome my enemies. If I stop them, they will return to slaughtering me. It has been said that the river called Sarsar was named so because of the sound of the running water in it, and that it is a verb derived from Sarrar, similar to the roaring wind. His saying: In unlucky days. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of unlucky days. Some of them said: It means successive ones. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: On unlucky days he said: consecutive days in which God sent down punishment. Others said: He meant the unlucky ones. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Unlucky days he said: Unlucky. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: In unlucky days are the days of God that were ominous for the people. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Nahsat means the ominous and unfortunate things. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, In unlucky days, he said: Days that are ominous for them. Others said: The meaning of this is: days of evil. It was mentioned that he said that: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding his statement: Unlucky days, he said: Unlucky means evil. An evil wind was sent upon them that did not contain any good. Others said: Unlucky: hardship. Mention of who said that: I was told by Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: In unlucky days. He said: Shaddad. The most correct of the sayings about this is the one that was said about me: unlucky days with bad luck, because that is the well-known meaning of bad luck in the speech of the Arabs. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of reciters in the regions, other than Nafi` and Abu `Amr, read it as fi ayyam nahsat with a kasra on the ha`. Nafi` and Abu `Amr read it as nahasat with a sukoon on the ha`. Abu `Amr, according to what was mentioned to us from him, provided evidence for his sukoon on the ha` by saying: a continuous unlucky day (al-Qamar 54:19) and that the ha` in it is sukoon. The correct thing to say about this is: They are two well-known readings, and each one of them has been read by knowledgeable readers, with their meanings agreeing. This is because moving the ha’ and sukoon on it in this are two well-known dialects. It is said: This is an unlucky day, and an unlucky day, with a kasra or sukoon on the ha’. Al-Farra’ said: Some Arabs recited to me: Inform Jutham and Lakhm that their brothers Tayy and Bahra are a people who are harmed by bad luck. As for stillness, it is the saying of God: An unlucky day (al-Qamar 54:19), and from it the saying of the rajaz poet: Two cloudy days and one sunny day, two lucky stars and one unlucky star So whoever has in his language an unlucky day (al-Qamar 54:19) said: In unlucky days, and whoever has in his language an unlucky day said: In unlucky days. Some of them said: Unlucky with a silent ha is the misfortune itself, and adding the day to unlucky is only adding to the misfortune, and unlucky with a broken ha is a description of the day as being unlucky, and for that reason it was said: In unlucky days because they are unlucky days. And His statement: We will make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, God Almighty says: And their punishment in the Hereafter will be more disgraceful for them and more severe in humiliation and degradation. And they will not be aided, He says: And they, meaning the ‘Ad tribe, will not be aided by God - on the Day of Resurrection when He punishes them - no helper will rescue them from Him, or take revenge for them.
41:17: God Almighty says: So We showed them the path of truth and the way of right guidance. As Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And as for Thamud, We guided them means We made clear to them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: As for Thamud, We guided them. We showed them the path of good and evil. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And as for Thamud, We guided them We made clear to them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And as for Thamud, We guided them, he said: We taught them guidance and misguidance, and We forbade them from following misguidance, and We commanded them to follow guidance. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement: Thamud. The majority of the reciters from the countries, except for Al-A’mash and Abdullah bin Abi Ishaq, read it with the nominative case of Thamud, and did not use it as a name for the nation known by that name. As for Al-A’mash, it is mentioned that he used to use that in the entire Qur’an except in His statement: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign. (al-Isra’ 17:59), as he did not use it in this particular place because in the script of the Qur’an in this place it is without an alif. He used to refer to Thamud as the name of a specific known man or the name of a known mountain. As for Ibn Ishaq, he used to read it in the accusative case. As for Thamud, without making a vowel, and even though this has a well-known meaning in Arabic, then what is more eloquent and more correct in grammar according to the people of Arabic is the nominative case to request the word as for from the nouns and that the verbs do not follow them. Rather, the Arabs use the verbs that come after the nouns in it if it is appropriate to place them before them, and the verb in as for is not appropriate to place it before the noun. Do you not see that it is not said: As for Thamud, we guided them as it is said: As for Thamud, we guided them? The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is to leave out the pronunciation. As for the nominative case, it is because it was described, and as for leaving out the pronunciation, it is because it is the name of the nation. His statement: So they preferred blindness over guidance means: So they chose blindness over the clarification that I made clear to them, and the guidance that I made known to them, by taking the path of misguidance over guidance, meaning over the clarification that I made clear to them of the Oneness of God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, They preferred blindness to guidance. He said: They chose misguidance and blindness over guidance. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: As for Thamud, We guided them, but they preferred blindness to guidance. He said: God sent messengers to them with guidance, but they preferred blindness to guidance. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So they preferred blindness. He said: We made it clear to them, and they preferred blindness to guidance. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: So they preferred blindness to guidance, he said: They preferred misguidance to guidance. And he recited: Thus have We made fair-seeming to every nation their deeds (al-An’am 6:108)… to the end of the verse. He said: So He made the ugly deeds of Thamud fair-seeming to him. And he recited: Then is he to whom the evil of his deed has been made fair-seeming so he sees it as good? Indeed, God sends astray whom He wills (Fatir 35:8)… to the end of the verse. His statement: So the thunderbolt of humiliating punishment seized them for what they had earned. He says: So it destroyed them with a humiliating and degrading punishment that humiliated and disgraced them. Humiliation means disgrace. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: The torment is humiliation. He said: humiliation. His saying: Because of what they were earning of sins by their disbelief in God before that, their opposition to Him, and their denial of His messengers.
41:18: And His statement: We saved those who believed means: We saved those who believed from the punishment that befell them because of their disbelief in God, those who believed in the Oneness of God and believed in His Messengers. And they were fearing God means: They were afraid that God would bring down upon them the punishment for their disbelief, as had befallen those of them who perished, if they had disbelieved. So they believed in meeting God and fearing His threat, and they believed in His Messengers, and they renounced the gods and rivals.
41:19: God Almighty says: And on the Day when these polytheists, the enemies of God, will be gathered together in the Fire, in the Fire of Hell, the first of them will be held back by the last of them. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: They will be distributed. He said: The first of them will be detained for the last of them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They will be distributed. He said: There will be a distribution among them, with the first of them returning to the last of them.
41:20: And His statement: Until, when they come to it, their hearing and their eyes will testify against them means: Until, when they come to the Fire, their hearing will testify against them because of what they used to listen to it in this world, and their eyes because of what they used to see and look at in this world, and their skins because of what they used to do. It has been said: What is meant by skins in this place is the vagina. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of al-Hakam al-Thaqafi, a man from the family of Abu Aqil, who traced the hadith back to the Prophet, And they said to their skins, ‘Why did you testify against us?’ He only meant their private parts, but he used a euphemism for them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Harmalah told us, that he heard Ubayd God ibn Abi Ja`far say: Until, when they come to it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them. He said: Their skins are the private parts. This statement that we mentioned from the one we mentioned about the meaning of skins, even if it is a meaning that can be interpreted, is not the most common meaning of skins nor the most well-known, and it is not permissible to transfer the meaning of that known thing to something that is closer to something else except with an argument that must be accepted.
41:21: God the Almighty says: And those who will be gathered to the Fire from among the enemies of God the Exalted will say to their skins when they testify against them regarding what they used to do in the world: Why did you testify against us regarding what we used to do in the world? Their skins will respond: God has made us speak, He who makes all things speak. So we spoke. He mentioned that these limbs will testify against their owners when God calls them to witness against them if they deny the actions they did in the world that angered God. This is what the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) reported. Mentioning the report that was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Ahmad bin Hazim Al-Ghifari narrated: Ali bin Qadim Al-Fazari narrated: Sharik narrated from Ubaid Al-Maktab from Al-Sha’bi from Anas who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) laughed one day until his molars were visible. Then he said: Will you not ask me why I laughed? They said: Why did I laugh, O Messenger of God? He said: I am amazed at the servant’s argument with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He said: He will say: O Lord, did You not promise me that You would not wrong me? He said: Then that is for You. He said: Then I do not accept any witness against me except from myself. He said: Is not me and the noble recording angels sufficient as witnesses? He said: Then his mouth will be sealed, and his limbs will speak of what he used to do. He said: Then he will say to them: Far from you and away from you, I used to argue. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Fadil ibn Amr, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, he said: Yahya bin Abi Bakr told us, on the authority of Shibl, he said: I heard Abu Qaz’ah telling Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Hakim bin Mu’awiyah, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said, and he pointed with his hand to the Levant, he said: Here to here you will be gathered, riding and walking, on your faces on the Day of Resurrection, on your mouths are the blood-stained ones. You will be seventy nations, you are the last of them and the most honored in the sight of God, and the first thing that will express itself from any one of you will be his thigh.” Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Al-Jariry told us, on the authority of Hakim bin Muawiyah, on the authority of his father, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: You will come on the Day of Resurrection with your mouths full of blood, and the first thing that will speak of a human being will be his thigh and his hand.” Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Bahz ibn Hakim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Why should I hold you back from the Fire? My Lord is calling and He will ask me, ‘Did I convey My worship?’ And I will say, ‘O Lord, I have conveyed it to them.’ So those of you who are present will convey it to those of you who are absent. Then you will be called with your mouths open in front of you. Then the first thing that will be revealed about any of you will be his thigh and his hand.” Muhammad bin Khalaf told me: Al-Haytham bin Kharijah told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Damdam bin Zar’ah, on the authority of Shureih bin Ubaid, on the authority of Uqbah: “He heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘The first bone in man to speak on the Day when mouths are sealed will be his left thigh.’” And His statement: And He created you the first time means that God Almighty says: And God created you the first creation when you were nothing, and to Him you will be returned means: And to Him is your destination after your death.
41:22: And you were not hiding in this world that your hearing, your sight, and your skins would testify against you on the Day of Resurrection. The commentators differed on the meaning of His statement: And you were not concealing. Some of them said: It means: And you were not concealing. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And what you were concealing means what you were deserving of from it. Others said: It means: And you were not fearing God. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And what you were concealing, he said: You were fearing God. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And you did not think. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And you were not covering up, he says: And you were not thinking that your hearing and your sight would testify against you, until he reached much of what you were doing. By God, O son of Adam, there are witnesses against you from your own body, not accused of anything, so watch them and fear God in your secret and public affairs, for nothing is hidden from Him. For Him, darkness is light, and for Him, the secret is public. So whoever is able to die while having good thoughts about God, let him do so, and there is no power except with God. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the one that says: The meaning of this is: And you were not concealing it, so you refrained from committing the forbidden acts of God in this world out of fear that your ears and eyes would testify against you today. We said that this is the most correct of the sayings on this matter, because the well-known meaning of concealment is hiding. If someone were to say: How can a person hide from himself what he does? It would be said: We have already explained that the meaning of that is only desires, and in his not doing it he is hiding it from himself. And His statement: But you thought that God did not know much of what you were doing. God Almighty says: But you thought, when you committed the sins of God in this world, that God did not know much of what you were doing of your evil deeds. That is why you did not conceal yourselves from your hearing, your sight, and your skins bearing witness against you, so you refrained from committing what God had forbidden you. He mentioned that this verse was revealed regarding a group of people who were arguing among themselves about God’s knowledge of what they were saying and were speaking in secret. The report mentioned that: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qat’i narrated: Abu Dawud narrated: Qais narrated: Mansur narrated: Mujahid narrated: Abu Muammar al-Azdi narrated: Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: I was hidden behind the curtains of the Ka’bah when three men entered: two Thaqafa’is and one Qurayshite, or two Qurayshites and one Thaqafa’i, with much fat on their bellies but little understanding in their hearts. They said something which I did not understand. One of them said: Do you think that God hears what we say? The two men said: If we raise our voices, He hears, but if we do not raise our voices, He does not hear. So I went to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and this verse was revealed: And you were not covering yourself lest your hearing and your sight should testify against you… to the end of the verse. Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated: Yahya ibn Saeed narrated: Sufyan narrated: Al-A’mash narrated: ‘Amara ibn ‘Umair narrated: Wahb ibn Rabi’ah narrated: ‘Abdullah ibn Mas’ud said: “I was concealed behind the curtains of the Ka’bah when three men, one from Thaqafi and the other from Quraysh, entered. They had little understanding in their hearts but much fat on their bellies. They began to discuss something among themselves. One of them said: ‘Do you think God hears what we say?’ The other said: ‘He hears when we raise our voices, but He does not hear when we lower them.’ The third said: ‘If He hears something from us, He hears it all.’ So I went to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and this verse was revealed: ‘And you were not covering yourselves lest your hearing and your sight should testify against you…’ until he reached: ‘And if they seek repentance, they will not be of those who are repented.’” Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Mansour told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah, something similar.
41:23: God the Almighty says: This which you had in this world, of your assumption that God does not know much of what you do of your ugly and bad deeds, is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord in this world. Ardakoum means He ruined you. It is said from this: Arda so-and-so did such-and-such: if He destroyed him, and Wardi is: if he perished, then he is ruined, and from this is the saying of Al-A’sha: During the circumambulation, I feared death, and how many have returned to their families without throwing stones? Meaning: How many people have lost their families without throwing stones? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, his statement: He destroyed you he said: He ruined you. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan recited: And that is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you, and said: People’s actions are only according to their assumptions about their Lord. As for the believer, he has good assumptions about God and thus does good deeds. As for the disbeliever and the hypocrite, he has bad assumptions and thus does bad deeds. Your Lord says: And you were not concealing yourself lest your ears and your eyes should testify against you, until He reached the losers. Muammar said: A man told me that a man will be ordered to the Fire, and he will turn around and say: O Lord, this was not my assumption of You. He will say: What was Your assumption of Me? He will say: I thought that You would forgive me and not punish me. He will say: I am as You think of Me. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Suspicion is of two types: Suspicion that saves and Suspicion that is rejected. Those who are certain that they will meet God (al-Baqarah 2:249) He said: Indeed, I thought that I would meet my account (al-Haqqah 69:20). This saving assumption is a certain assumption. And here He said: And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord that has ruined you. This is a rejected assumption. And His statement: We only assume an assumption, and we are not certain (al-Jathiyah 45:32) “And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say and narrate that from his Lord: ‘My servant is according to his assumption of Me, and I am with him when he calls upon Me.’” The place of His statement: That is you is in the nominative case with His statement: your assumption. If that is the case, then His statement: He destroyed you is in the accusative case, meaning: He destroyed you. It may also be possible that it is in the nominative case by resumption, meaning: He destroyed you, as He said: These are the verses of the Wise Book, guidance and mercy (Luqman 31:2-3) in the reading of those who read it in the nominative case. The meaning of the statement is: This assumption that you assumed about your Lord, that He does not know much of what you do, is what destroyed you, because because of this assumption you dared to transgress the prohibitions of God and committed them, and did what God forbade you from, so that destroyed you and ruined you. So you have become among the losers. He says: So today you have become among the ruined, and you have been deceived by selling your homes in Paradise for the homes of the people of Paradise in Hell.
41:24: God the Most High says: If these people who will be herded into the Fire are patient in the Fire, then the Fire will be their dwelling place and abode. And if they seek repentance means that they will be returned to the One they love by having their punishment lightened. They will not be among those who will be repented means that they will not be among those who will be returned to Paradise, so that the punishment they are in will be lightened. This is like the statement of God the Most High, informing us about them: They will say, ‘Our Lord, our wretchedness has overcome us’ (Al-Mu’minun 23:106)… until His statement: And do not speak to Us (Al-Mu’minun 23:108), and like their statement to the keepers of Hell: Call upon your Lord to lighten for us a day of the punishment (Ghafir 40:49) until His statement: And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error (Ghafir 40:50).
41:25: He, the Most High, meant by His saying: And We appointed for them companions, and We sent to them companions from among the devils, and We made them companions for them. We paired them with them, making their ugly deeds seem good to them, so they made that seem good to them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And We appointed for them companions, he said: Satan. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And We have appointed for them companions, he said: devils. And His statement: And they made attractive to them what is before them and what is behind them means: So their companions from among the devils made attractive to these disbelievers what is before them of worldly matters, so they made that attractive to them and made it beloved to them until they preferred it over matters of the Hereafter. And what is behind them means: And they also made attractive to them what is after their death by calling them to deny the Resurrection, and that whoever among them is destroyed will not be resurrected, and that there is no reward or punishment until they believed them in that, and it became easy for them to do whatever they desired, and to commit all the indecencies they enjoyed by making that attractive to themselves. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, So they made attractive to them what was before them of the affairs of this world, and what was behind them of the affairs of the Hereafter. And His statement: And the word has come into effect upon them means that God Almighty says: And the punishment has become obligatory for them because they have ridden in what their companions have made attractive to them, and they are from among the devils. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: And the word has come into effect upon them he said: the punishment among nations that have passed on before them of jinn and mankind God Almighty says: And it has come into effect upon these people for whom We appointed companions from among the devils, who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, the punishment among nations that have passed on before them of their like. It has come into effect upon them from Our punishment like that which has come into effect upon these people, some of them from among the jinn and some of them from among mankind. Indeed, they were losers He says: Indeed, those nations upon whom Our punishment has come into effect from among the jinn and mankind were deceived by their exchanging the pleasure and mercy of God for His wrath and punishment.
41:26: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger from the polytheists of Quraysh said: Do not listen to this Qur’an and make noise during it. That is, they said to those of their allies from the polytheists who obeyed them: Do not listen to the reciter of this Qur’an when he recites it, and do not pay attention to him, and do not follow what is in it and act upon it. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it that you may overcome.’ He said: This is the saying of the polytheists. They said: Do not follow this Qur’an and be distracted from it. His saying: And cover it up with false speech means: Cover it up with false speech when you hear someone reciting it so that you do not hear him or understand what is in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God: Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it, he said: The bleating and whistling, and mixing up speech about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited, the Quraysh used to do it. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And they made noises during it, he said: By bleating, whistling, and mixing up speech when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an, the Quraysh used to do it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Do not listen to this Qur’an and speak noisily during it’: meaning, they denied it, rejected it, and opposed it. He said: This is the statement of the polytheists of the Arabs. Abu Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Some of them said regarding His statement: And speak noisily therein, that they should talk and shout so that you will not hear him. And his saying: Perhaps you will prevail means: Perhaps by your action you will prevent those who want to listen to him from listening to him, so that they will not hear him, and if they do not hear him or understand him, they will not follow him. Thus, by your action you will prevail over Muhammad.
41:27: God Almighty said: Then We will make those who disbelieved in God from the polytheists of Quraysh who said this statement taste a severe punishment in the Hereafter and We will recompense them with the worst of what they used to do meaning: We will reward them for doing this and other actions with the worst recompense for the actions they did in this world.
41:28: God the Most High says: This is the recompense with which these disbelievers from among the polytheists of Quraysh will be recompensed, the recompense of the enemies of God. Then God the Most High began to describe the description of that recompense and what it is, saying: It is the Fire. So the Fire is an explanation of the recompense and a translation of it, and it is raised by responding to it. Then He said: For them therein is the home of eternity, meaning for these polytheists in the Fire is the home of eternity, meaning the home of staying and remaining, without end or time. The home that God the Most High informed them that they will have in the Fire is the Fire, and that is appropriate due to the difference in the two words, just as it is said to you from your town, a righteous home, and from Kufa, a noble home, and the home is Kufa and the town, so that is appropriate due to the difference in the words. It was mentioned to us that in the reading of Ibn Mas`ud, it is: That is the recompense of the enemies of God, the Fire, the home of eternity. So in that is the correction of what we said about the interpretation of that, and that is because he translated the home from the Fire. And His statement: As a reward for their denial of Our signs, meaning: We did what We did to these people by punishing them with the Fire for their actions as a reward from Us for their denial in this world of Our signs that We used as evidence against them.
41:29: God Almighty says: And those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger will say on the Day of Resurrection after He has put them into Hell: O our Lord, show us those who led us astray from among Your creation of jinn and humans. And it was said: The one who He is from the jinn, Iblis, who is from the human being, the son of Adam, who killed his brother. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Haddad, on the authority of Hubbah al-Arni, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: Show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind, he said: Abtis the devils and the son of Adam who killed his brother. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Malik ibn Husayn, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, regarding his statement: Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind, he said: Satan and the son of Adam who killed his brother. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Wahb bin Jarir told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhayl, on the authority of Abu Malik and Ibn Malik, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him: Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind. He said: The son of Adam who killed his brother, and Iblis is the devil. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, regarding His statement: Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind... the verse, that they are the son of Adam, the murderer, and Iblis, the devil. As for the son of Adam, every person who commits a major sin will call upon him and will enter Hellfire because of his call. As for Iblis, every person who commits polytheism will call upon him and they will both be in Hellfire. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada: Our Lord, show us those who led us astray among the jinn and mankind refers to Satan and the son of Adam who killed his brother. And His statement: We will place them under our feet so that they will be among the lowest. He says: We will place these two who led us astray under our feet, because the gates of Hell are lower than each other, and whoever is lower than it is more severe for his people, and the punishment of his people is more severe. Therefore, the disbelievers asked their Lord to show them the two who led them astray so that they would be lower than them so that they would be in the most severe punishment in the lowest level of Hell.
41:30: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ alone, with no partner, and disavow all gods and rivals, then remained steadfast on the oneness of God, and did not mix the oneness of God with associating others with Him, and ended up obeying Him in what He commanded and forbade. In a similar manner to what we have said about this, the report came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the people of interpretation said it with their differences, regarding the meaning of his saying: Then they were steadfast, mentioning the report about that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Amr bin Ali told us: Salim bin Qutaybah Abu Qutaybah told us: Suhayl bin Abi Hazm al-Qat’i told us, on the authority of Thabit al-Bunani, on the authority of Anas bin Malik that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: The people said it, then most of them disbelieved, so whoever dies upon it is among those who remain steadfast. Some of them said: It means: They did not associate anything with Him, but they remained committed to monotheism. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Amir ibn Sa`d, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Imran, he said: I read this verse in the presence of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They are those who do not associate anything with God. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, with his chain of transmission, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, the same. He said: Jarir bin Abdul Hamid and Abdullah bin Idris narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Musa, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq, may God be pleased with him, that he said to his companions: Those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They said, “Our Lord is God,’ and then acted upon it. He said: You have interpreted it in the wrong way. “Those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast” are those who did not equate it with polytheism or anything else. Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal al-Maharibi, who said: Abu Bakr said: What do you say about this verse: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: So they said, Our Lord is God, and then remained steadfast from sin. Abu Bakr said: You have taken it upon yourself in the wrong context. They said, Our Lord is God, and then remained steadfast, and did not turn to any god other than Him. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Layth, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain on a right course, he said: meaning, on: There is no god but God. He said: Hakam told us on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They submitted and did not associate partners with Him until they joined Him. He said: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They are those who said, Our Lord is God, and then did not associate anything with Him until they joined Him. He said: Hakam told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Jami’ bin Shaddad, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, the same. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain on a right course, he said: They continued on that. Saad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Hafs bin Omar told us: Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us on the authority of Ikrimah regarding his statement: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They remained steadfast in testifying that there is no god but God. Others said: The meaning of this is: Then they remained steadfast in obeying him. It was mentioned that he said that: Ahmad bin Mani’ told us, he said: Abdullah bin Mubarak told us, he said: Yunus bin Yazid told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: Omar, may God be pleased with him, recited on the pulpit, Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They remained steadfast by God’s obedience, and they did not swerve like a fox. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: They remained steadfast in obeying God. When al-Hasan recited it, he would say: O God, You are our Lord, so grant us steadfastness. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, meaning: in performing His obligatory duties. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, those who say, ‘Our Lord is God,’ and then remain steadfast, he said: in the worship of God and in obedience to Him. His saying: The angels descend upon them means: The angels descend upon them when death descends upon them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The angels will descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve,’ he said: at death. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, The angels descend upon them. He said: At death. His saying: That you should not fear and not grieve means: The angels will descend upon them, telling them not to fear and not to grieve. So that is in the accusative case if that is its meaning.
