It was reported that Abdullah used to recite this verse: The angels will descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve.’ Meaning: They will descend upon them, saying, Do not fear and do not grieve. What he meant by Do not fear is what you will do after your death, and Do not grieve about what you will leave behind. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, That you do not fear and do not grieve. He said: Do not fear what is before you, and do not grieve over what is after you. Yunus told me: Yahya bin Hassan told us, on the authority of Muslim bin Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The angels will descend upon them, [saying], ‘Do not fear and do not grieve.’ He said: Do not fear what you will face in the Hereafter, and do not grieve over what you have left behind of your worldly life, of family and children, for We will replace all of that for you. It was said: That is in the afterlife. Mention of the one who said that: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: The angels will descend upon them, saying, ‘Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good tidings of Paradise.’ That is in the Hereafter. And His statement: And be glad with the Paradise which you were promised. He says: And be happy that in the Hereafter you will have the Paradise which you were promised in this world because of your faith in God and your steadfastness in obeying Him. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And receive good tidings of Paradise, which you were promised in this world.
41:31: God Almighty says, informing us about what His angels say when they descend upon these believers who were steadfast in obeying Him at the time of their death: We are your allies O people, in the life of this world We were their guardians therein. He also mentioned that they are the guardians who record their deeds. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, We are your guardians in the life of this world. We are the guardians who were with you in this world, and we are your guardians in the Hereafter. His statement, And in the Hereafter, means: In the Hereafter also, We are your guardians, just as We were your guardians in this world. And you will have therein whatever your souls desire, means: And you will have in the Hereafter with God whatever your souls desire of pleasures and desires. His statement, And you will have therein whatever you request, means: And you will have in the Hereafter whatever you request.
41:32: And His statement: A lodging from a Forgiving, Most Merciful means: Your Lord has given you that as a lodging for you from a Lord who is Forgiving of your sins, Merciful to you, that He should not punish you after your repentance. And He placed nuzul in the accusative case as a source of the meaning of His statement: And therein you will have whatever your souls desire, and therein you will have whatever you request because in that is the interpretation that your Lord has sent you down with whatever you desire of bliss as a lodging.
41:33: God Almighty says: Who is better in speech, O people, than one who says, Our Lord is God, then remains steadfast in belief in Him, adheres to His commands and prohibitions, and calls the servants of God to what he said and acts upon it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, he said: Al-Hasan recited: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims.’ He said: This is the beloved of God, this is the friend of God, this is the chosen one of God, this is the best of God, this is the most beloved of creation to God. God answered his call, and he invited people to what God answered of his call, and he did righteousness in answering it, and he said, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims.’ This is the caliph of God. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God... the verse, he said: This is a servant whose words are true to his actions, whose income is his exit, whose secret is his public, and whose witness is his unseen. And the hypocrite is a servant whose words contradict his actions, whose income is his exit, whose secret is his public, and whose witness is his unseen. Scholars differed about who was meant by this description of people. Some of them said: It refers to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mention of who said that: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And who is better in speech than one who invites to God? He said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he called to Islam. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And who is better in speech than one who invites to God and does righteousness and says, ‘Indeed, I am of the Muslims,’ he said: This is the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Others said: It refers to the muezzin. It was mentioned that he said that: Dawud bin Sulayman bin Yazid al-Maktab al-Basri told me, he said: Amr bin Jarir al-Bajali told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qais bin Abi Hazim, regarding the statement of God, And who is better in speech than one who invites to God, he said: The muezzin, and does righteousness, he said: The prayer is between the call to prayer and the iqamah. His saying: And he said, ‘I am one of the Muslims,’ means: He said: I am one of those who submitted to God through obedience, humbled themselves before Him through worship, and humbled themselves before Him through belief in His Oneness.
41:34: And His statement: And not equal are the good deed and the bad means that the Most High says: The good deed of those who said, Our Lord is God and then remained steadfast, so they spoke well and responded to their Lord in what He called them to of obedience to Him, and called the servants of God to the same as they responded to their Lord, is not equal to the bad deed of those who said, Do not listen to this Qur'an and speak noisily during it that you may overcome. Likewise, their conditions and stations are not equal before God, but they differ, as He, the Most High, described that He distinguished between them. And He, the Most High, said: And not equal are the good deed and the bad deed. So He repeated la, meaning: The good deed and the bad deed are not equal, because everything that is not equal to something, the thing to which it is related is not equal to it, just as everything that is equal to something, the other thing to which it is related is equal to it. So it is said: So-and-so is equal to so-and-so, and so-and-so is equal to him. Likewise, so-and-so is not equal to so-and-so, nor is so-and-so equal to him. For this reason, la was repeated with the bad deed, and if it had not been repeated with it, the statement would have been correct. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It is permissible to say that the second is redundant, meaning: Abdullah and Zaid are not the same, so the la was added for emphasis, as he said: {Lest the People of the Scripture know that they are not able} (al-Hadid 57:29): meaning so that he knows, and as he said: {Lest the People of the Scripture know that they are not able}, and in his statement: {I do not swear} he says: The second la in his statement: {Lest the People of the Scripture know that they are not able} was returned to its place, because the negation was attached to the word they are able and not the word knowledge, as it is said: I do not think that Zaid will not stand, meaning: I think that Zaid will not stand. He said: And sometimes they were certain, so they brought it first and last, and sometimes they were satisfied with the first of the second. It was reported that it was heard from the Arabs: Ma ka’anī ‘arfha I do not know her, meaning as if I do not know her. He said: As for the la in his statement: {I do not swear}, it is only an answer, and the oath after it is a new sentence, and the letter of negation is not a subject or a relative clause. What he meant by his saying: Good and bad are not equal is that belief in God and working to obey Him are not equal, and associating partners with Him and working to disobey Him are not equal. And His saying: Repel evil with that which is better means that God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, repel with your patience the ignorance of those who have been ignorant of you, and with your forgiveness of those who have wronged you the wrong of the wrongdoer, and with your patience with them the harm you find from them and that you encounter from them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with their differences in their interpretation. Mention of those who said that: Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Repel evil with that which is better, he said: God commanded the believers to be patient when angry, and to be forbearing and forgiving when wronged. If they do that, God will protect them from Satan, and their enemy will submit to them, as if he were a close friend. Others said: The meaning of this is: Repay with peace the one who wronged you with his wrong. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata’, Repel evil with that which is better, he said: with peace. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid: Repel evil with that which is better. He said: Peace be upon you when you meet him. And His statement: Then he between whom and you there was enmity will become as though he was a devoted friend. God Almighty says: Do this that I have commanded you to do, O Muhammad, by repelling the evil of the one who wronged you with the kindness that I have commanded you to do to him, so that the one who wronged you, between whom and you there was enmity, will become as though he were, due to his kindness to you, a devoted friend of yours from among your cousins, close to you in relation. And the devoted friend is the one who is close. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, As if he were a close friend: meaning as if he were a close friend.
41:35: God Almighty says: And none can repel evil with good except those who are patient for God's sake over hardships and difficult matters. And He said: and what he encounters and did not say: and what he encounters, because the meaning of the statement is: and what he encounters this action of repelling evil with what is better. And His saying: And none receives it except one who has a great portion, meaning: And none receives this except one who has a great portion and has been a forerunner in doing good deeds. As Muhammad urged us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And none will attain it except one of great fortune: one of great fortune. It was said: The portion that God Almighty mentioned in this verse is for these people is Paradise. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And none will attain it except those who are patient... the verse and the great portion: Paradise. “It was mentioned to us that a man insulted Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him and the Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was present, so he forgave him for a moment. Then Abu Bakr became furious and retaliated. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) stood up and Abu Bakr followed him and said: O Messenger of God, the man insulted me, and I forgave and pardoned you while you were sitting. When you tried to retaliate, you stood up, O Prophet of God. The Prophet of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: An angel was defending you, but when you were about to retaliate, the angel left and Satan came. By God, I would not sit with Satan, O Abu Bakr.” Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And none will receive it except those who are patient, and none will receive it except one with great good fortune, meaning: those for whom God has prepared Paradise.
41:36: And His statement: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, then seek refuge in God... the verse. God the Almighty says: And if Satan, O Muhammad, should cast into your soul an evil whisper from the inner conversation, wanting to make you repay the wrongdoer with evil, and inviting you to harm him, then seek refuge in God and protect yourself from his steps. Indeed, God is the All-Hearing of your seeking refuge from him and your protection with Him from his evil suggestions, and of other words of yours and the words of others. He is the All-Knowing of what he casts into your soul of his suggestions, and what your soul tells you and what he removes from your heart, and other matters of your affairs and the affairs of His creation. Muhammad told us, saying: Ahmad told us, saying: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: But if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, he said: a whisper and self-talk, then seek refuge in God from Satan, the accursed. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And if an evil suggestion comes to you from Satan, he said: This is anger.
41:37: God Almighty says: Among the proofs of God Almighty to His creation and His evidence of His Oneness and the greatness of His power is the alternation of night and day, and the punishment of each one of them by its companion, and the sun and the moon. The sun does not overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, each in an orbit is floating. (Ya-Sin 36:40) Do not prostrate, O people, to the sun or the moon, for even if they move in the orbit for your benefit, they only move for you because God makes them move for you, obedient to Him in their movement and course, not because they are able to move and course by themselves without God making them move and course, or because they are able to benefit or harm you. Rather, God has subjected them to you for your benefit and interests, so prostrate to Him, and worship Him instead of them, for if He wills, He will extinguish their light, leaving you confused in darkness, unable to find a way, and unable to see anything. It was said: Prostrate to God who created them. So it was made plural with the letter ha and the letter nun, because what is meant by the speech is: And prostrate to God who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon. And that is a plural, and you are their pronoun, even though it is the custom of the Arabs, when they pluralize a male to a female, to pronounce their pronoun with the wording of the pronoun of the masculine, so they say: Your two brothers and your two sisters spoke to me, and they do not say: He spoke to me, because it is their custom to feminize the report of males other than the sons of Adam in the plural, so they say: I saw with Amr some clothes, so I took them from him, and I liked the rings of Zaid, so I bought them from him. His statement: If you worship Him, means: If you worship God and submit to Him through obedience, and part of obeying Him is that you devote your worship to Him alone, and do not associate anything other than Him in your obedience to Him and your worship of Him, because worship is not suitable for anyone other than Him and is not appropriate for anything other than Him.
41:38: God Almighty says: If, O Muhammad, those among whom you are, the polytheists of Quraysh, are too arrogant to prostrate to God, who created them and created the sun and the moon, then the angels who are with your Lord are not too arrogant to do that, nor do they feel too arrogant to do so. Rather, they glorify Him and pray night and day, and they do not get tired: He says: They do not slacken in their worship, nor do they get tired of praying to Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: But if they are arrogant, then those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day. He said: He means Muhammad, he says: My servants are angels in rows, glorifying Him and not being arrogant.
41:39: God Almighty says: Among God’s proofs and evidence of His ability to resurrect the dead after their affliction, and restore them to their original state after their destruction, is that you, O Muhammad, see the earth as barren and dusty, with no plants or crops on it. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren meaning dusty and crumbling. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And among His signs is that you see the earth barren. He said: Dry and crumbling. But when We send down upon it rain, it quivers. God Almighty says: So when We send down from the sky rain upon this barren earth, it quivers with vegetation. He says: It moves with it. Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Shaken he said: With plants. And swelled he said: Swelled. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And it swelled means it became puffy. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: So when We send down water upon it, it quivers and swells. The rain is known by its abundance and its swell. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And it grew for the plant, he said: It rose before it grew. And His statement: Indeed, He who revives it will revive the dead. God Almighty says: Indeed, He who revives this barren land, bringing forth vegetation from it, and making it vibrate with crops after it had dried up and been covered with rain that He sent down upon it, is able to revive the dead of the children of Adam after their death with the water that He sends down from the sky to revive them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said: Just as He revives the earth with rain, so He revives the dead with water on the Day of Resurrection between the two blasts. He meant by that the interpretation of His statement: Indeed, He who revives it will revive the dead. And His saying: He is over all things competent, God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, is capable of reviving His creation after their death and of doing whatever He wills. Nothing He wills is beyond His power, and nothing He wills is impossible for Him to do.
41:40: He, the Most High, means by His saying: Indeed, those who dispute concerning Our verses: those who deviate from the truth in Our arguments and proofs, and turn away from them, denying and rejecting them. I have previously explained the meaning of the grave with sufficient evidence that does not need to be repeated here. We will now mention some of the differences of opinion regarding what is meant by it in this context. The interpreters differed about what is meant by the meaning of atheism in this passage. Some of them said: It means the polytheists opposing the Qur’an with noise and whistling in mockery of it. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who blaspheme concerning Our verses, he said: Al-Maka’ and what was mentioned with it. Some of them said: It is meant to inform about their lies regarding the verses of God. Mention of who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses he said: They lie about Our verses. Others said: It means they are stubborn. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses he said: They are disobedient: they are stubborn. Others said: It means disbelief and polytheism. Mention of those who said that: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Indeed, those who dispute concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us, he said: These are the people of polytheism. And he said: Disbelief means disbelief and polytheism. Others said: It is meant to inform about their changing the meanings of the Book of God. Those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Indeed, those who err concerning Our verses are not hidden from Us, he said: It means putting words in the wrong place. All of these sayings that we have mentioned in interpretation of that are close in meaning, because lahd and ilhad mean to turn away, and it may be a turn away from the verses of God, and a deviation from them by denying them, and it may be by mockery, bleating and clapping, and it may be a separation from them and stubbornness, and it may be a distortion of them and a change in their meanings. There is no statement more correct than what we have said, and the report about them being blasphemous regarding the verses of God should be general, just as our Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, has made that general. And His statement: They are not hidden from Us means that God the Almighty says: We are All-Knowing of them, and they are not hidden from Us, and We are watching them when they come to Us. This is a threat from God the Almighty to them when He says: They will know when they come to Us what painful punishment they will encounter. Then God the Almighty informs us of what He will do to them when they come to Him, saying: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better or he who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? God the Almighty says: For these people who dispute Our signs today, there will be the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection. Then God says: Is he who is thrown into the Fire better, or he who comes on the Day of Resurrection secure from the punishment of God because of his belief in God the Almighty? This is the disbeliever. If he believes in the signs of God and follows His commands and prohibitions, He will make him safe on the Day of Resurrection from what He warned him of of His punishment if he comes to Him that day as a disbeliever. His saying: Do whatever you want. This is also a threat to them from God that came out as a command, and this is what Mujahid used to say. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Do whatever you want. He said: This is a threat. And His saying: He is Seeing of what you do, God Almighty says: O people, God is All-Knowing of the deeds that you do, and nothing of them or anything else is hidden from Him.
41:41: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who denied this Qur’an and belied it when it came to them. And what is meant by the mention is the Qur’an. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them disbelieved in the Qur’an. And His statement: And indeed, it is a noble Book, God Almighty says: And indeed, this Reminder is a noble Book, by God’s honoring of it and protecting it from anyone who wanted to change it, distort it, or alter it, whether human, jinn, or rebellious devil. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: And indeed, it is a noble Book, meaning: God made it noble because it is His speech, and He protected it from falsehood. Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And indeed, it is a precious Book. He said: Precious from Satan.
41:42: And His statement: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said that its meaning is: denunciation cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. Mention of those who said that: Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Sa’id, Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. He said: Denunciation from before it or from behind it. Others said: The meaning of this is: Satan cannot subtract any truth from it, nor add any falsehood to it. They said: And falsehood is Satan. His saying: from before him from the side of the truth, nor from behind him from the side of falsehood. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. Falsehood: Satan is unable to subtract from it the truth, nor add to it falsehood. Others said: Its meaning is that falsehood cannot add any letters to it nor subtract any of them. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, Falsehood cannot come to it from before it or from behind it. He said: Falsehood is Satan, he cannot add a letter to it or subtract from it. The first and most correct of the sayings about this, in our view, is to say: Its meaning is that the one with falsehood cannot, by his trickery, change it, or alter any of its meanings from what it is, and that is coming from before it, nor can he attach to it what is not from it, and that is coming from behind it. And His statement: A revelation from a Wise, Praiseworthy One. God Almighty says: It is a revelation from the One with wisdom to manage His servants and direct them to what is in their best interests. Praiseworthy: He says: Praised for His blessings upon them by His favors upon them.
41:43: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: These polytheists who deny what you have brought to them from your Lord say to you only what the nations before them said to their messengers who were before you. He says to him: So be patient over the harm they inflict upon you, just as the messengers of strong will were patient. And do not be like the companion of the fish. (al-Qalam
41:44: God Almighty says: And if We had made this Qur’an which We have revealed, O Muhammad, foreign, your people of Quraysh would have met you. Why were its verses not explained in detail? Meaning: Why were its evidence and the verses in it not explained, so that we might understand it and know what it is and what is in it? Is it foreign? Meaning that they would have said in denial of it: Is this Qur’an foreign, and the language of the one to whom it was revealed is Arabic? And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, that he said about this verse, Why are its verses not explained in detail? [Are they] a foreign language and an Arab? He said: If this Qur’an were a foreign language, they would have said that the Qur’an is a foreign language, and Muhammad is an Arab. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Abi Uday told me, on the authority of Dawud ibn Abi Hind, on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi Wahshiyah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: Why are His verses not explained in detail? A foreigner and an Arab? He said: The Messenger is an Arab, but the language is foreign. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding His statement: And if We had made it a foreign Qur’an, they would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail?’ [A foreign language and an Arabic one]? A foreign Qur’an and an Arabic tongue. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Abi Musa, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Mut’i’, in a similar manner. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: Why were His verses not explained in detail? So he made an Arab whose speech was foreign and an Arab whose man was Arab. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement: And if We had made it a foreign Qur’an, they would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail?’ He said: Its verses were explained. Is it foreign and Arabic? We are an Arab people. What do we have to do with foreignness? Others have contradicted this statement that we mentioned about them, and they said: The meaning of that is Why were His verses not explained in detail? Some of them are Arabic and some of them are foreign. This interpretation is based on the interpretation of those who read foreign by leaving out the interrogative in it and making it a report from God Almighty about what the polytheists said, meaning: Why were His verses not explained in detail, some of them foreign that the foreigners know, and some of them Arabic that the Arabs understand. Those who said that: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yaqub narrated to us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: Quraysh said, Why was this Qur’an not revealed in both Arabic and foreign languages? So God revealed, They would have said, ‘Why are its verses not explained in detail? [Among them] a foreign language and an Arab?’ Say, ‘It is, for those who believe, a guide and a healing.’ Then God revealed after this verse, For every language, there are stones of baked clay. (Hud 11:82-15:74) He said: Persian, you have Arabized your age and all. The reciters of the regions read, Among them a foreign language and an Arab? as a question. It was reported on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read it as a foreign language with one hamza, not as a question, in the meaning we mentioned on the authority of Ja`far ibn Abi Al-Mughira, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr. The correct reading in this regard, according to us, is the reading that the readers of the countries follow, due to the consensus of the evidence on it, based on the method of interrogation. And His statement: “Say: It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure.” God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to them: It - and by His statement: It he means the Qur’an - is, for those who believe in God and His Messenger, and believe in what he brought them from their Lord, a guide meaning an explanation of the truth and a cure meaning that it is a cure from ignorance. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Say: It is for those who believe, a guide and a cure.” He said: God made it a light, a blessing, and a cure for the believers. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, “Say: It is, for those who believe, a guide and a cure.” He said: The Qur’an. And His statement: And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness upon them. God Almighty says: And those who do not believe in God and His Messenger, and what He brought them from God is in their ears a weight on them from listening to this Qur’an, and a deafness so that they do not listen to it but turn away from it, and it is blindness upon them. He says: And this Qur’an is upon the hearts of those who disbelieve in it, blindness to it, so they do not see its arguments against them, and what it contains of admonitions. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness and it is blindness upon them. They are blind and deaf to the Qur’an, so they do not benefit from it, nor do they desire it. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And those who do not believe - in their ears is deafness He said: Deafness and it is blindness to them He said: Their hearts are blind to it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And it is blindness to them, he said: Blindness is disbelief. The reciters of the regions read And He is blind to them with a fat-ha on the meem. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he read And He is blind to them with a kasra on the meem as a description of the Qur'an. The correct reading for us is what the readers of the countries do. And His statement: Those are the ones who are calling from a distant place. The people of interpretation differed about its meaning. Some of them said: The meaning of that is that God, may He be glorified and exalted, likened the blindness of their hearts to understanding what He revealed in the Qur’an of His proofs and admonitions to something distant in understanding, like someone who hears a voice from far away being called, but does not understand what he was called to, like the Arabs saying to a man of little understanding: You are calling from far away, and like their saying to understanding: You are taking matters from close by. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Mujahid, Those will be called from a place far away. He said: Far from their hearts. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: Those will be called from a distant place, he said: They neglected to accept the command from a nearby place, to repent and believe, so that it would be accepted from them, but they refused. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they will be called on the Day of Resurrection from a place far away from them by their most hideous names. Mention of those who said that: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ajlah, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, Those are the ones who call from a distant place. He said: The man calls out with his most hideous name. The Arabists differed about the place of the completion of his statement: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them, so some of them said that its completion is Those are being called from a place far away, and those who said this made the predicate of Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message “Those are being called from a place far away,” and some of the grammarians of Basra said: This is permissible, and it is permissible for it to be based on the report of the Qur’an that can be dispensed with, just as things dispense with the report if the speech is long and the meaning is known, like his statement: And if only a Qur’an by which mountains could be moved or the earth could be split apart (al-Ra’d 13:31) and what is similar to that. He said: A sheikh from the people of knowledge told me, he said: I heard Isa bin Omar asking Amr bin Ubaid, Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them, where is its information? Amr said, its meaning in the interpretation is: Indeed, those who disbelieved in the message when it came to them disbelieved in it. And indeed, it is a noble Book. Isa said: You did well, O Abu Uthman. Some of the grammarians of Kufa used to say: If you wish, you can make the answer to Indeed, those who disbelieve in the message “Those are called from a distant place.” And if you wish, its answer would be in His saying: And indeed, it is a noble Book. So its answer would be known, so it was left out, and it would be more expressive of the two faces and more similar to what came in the Qur’an. Others said: Rather, this is because it was diverted from the report of what it began with to the report of what came after it from the remembrance. So, according to this statement, the report of those who disbelieved in the remembrance was left out, and the report of the remembrance was made, so its completion, according to this statement, is: And indeed, it is a noble Book. So the meaning of the statement, according to the one who said this statement, was: Indeed, the remembrance that these polytheists disbelieved in when it came to them, and indeed, it is a noble Book. And he likened it to His statement: And those among you who die and leave wives behind them, they shall wait concerning themselves (al-Baqarah 2:234). The most correct of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is to say: It is one of the things whose report was left out, as it was sufficient for the listeners to know its meaning, since the speech was prolonged.
41:45: God Almighty says: And We gave Moses the Scripture, O Muhammad, meaning the Torah, just as We gave you the Criterion, but they differed concerning it, meaning: those of the Jews who were given it differed concerning the actions in it. And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been judged between them, meaning: and had it not been for what preceded of God’s judgment and ruling concerning them, that He delayed their punishment until the Day of Resurrection, it would have been judged between them. He says: He would have hastened the decision between them concerning what they differed concerning by destroying the falsifiers among them. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, he said: They would have been delayed until the Day of Resurrection. His statement: And indeed, they are in disturbing doubt about it. He says: And the group of them who are falsifying is in disturbing doubt about what they said about it. He says: What they said about it makes them doubtful, because they said it without proof, and they only said it based on conjecture.
41:46: God the Almighty says: Whoever does an act of obedience to God in this world, obeying His command, and refraining from what He has forbidden, does it for his own soul meaning: he did that righteous deed for his own soul, because he will be rewarded for it, and will deserve Paradise from God in the Hereafter, and salvation from the Fire. But whoever does evil, it is against himself meaning: whoever commits sins against God in this world, it is against himself, because he has earned God’s wrath and painful punishment for it. And your Lord is not unjust to His servants God the Almighty says: And your Lord, O Muhammad, does not carry the punishment for a sin of a sinner for something he did not earn. Rather, He does not punish anyone except for the crime he earned in this world, or for a reason by which he deserved it. And God knows best.
41:47: God Almighty says: To God do those who know Him refer the knowledge of the Hour, for no one knows when it will occur except Him. And no fruits emerge from their coverings He says: And no fruit of a tree emerges from its coverings in which it is hidden, emerging from it prominently. And no female conceives He says: And no female conceives from a pregnancy when she conceives, nor gives birth to her child except with the knowledge of God, nothing of that is hidden from Him. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement: And no fruits come forth from their coverings, the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: from its sleeves, he said: when it appears. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi, And whatever fruits come forth from their coverings, he said: from its ripening. The coverings are the plural of kammah, which is every container for water or other things. The Arabs call the peel of the kaffara kamm. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement: from the fruits. The reciters of Medina recited it as from the fruits in the plural, and the reciters of Kufa recited it as from the fruit in the singular. Whichever of the two recitations it was recited with is correct in our view, due to the similarity of their meanings and their fame in recitation. And His statement: And the Day He will call to them, ‘Where are My partners?’ God Almighty says: And the Day God will call to these polytheists who associated with Him in this world, the idols and statues: Where are My partners whom you associated with Me in your worship? They will say, We have informed you, meaning, We have informed you, “There is not one of us who will bear witness that You have a partner.” He says: These polytheists will say to their Lord on that day: There is not one of us who will bear witness that You have a partner. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of who said that: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: We informed you means: We informed you. Muhammad told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: We have given you permission, none of us is a witness, they said: We have obeyed you, none of us is a witness, on the basis that you have a partner.
41:48: God Almighty says: On the Day of Resurrection, the gods they used to worship in this world will be lost to these polytheists, and they will be led astray by a path other than theirs. They will not benefit them, nor will they protect them from any of God’s punishment that has befallen them. His statement: And they thought they had no escape, meaning: And they were certain then that they had no refuge, meaning they had no refuge to which they could turn from God’s punishment. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, And they thought they had no escape: they were certain that they had no refuge. The Arab scholars differed about the meaning for which the function of doubt was invalidated in this instance. Some of the people of Basra said: He did that because the meaning of his saying, and they thought is: they were certain. He said: And here, ‘ma’ is a particle and not a noun, and the verb does not function in such a case, so the verb was made invalidated. Some of them said: A verb is not invalidated while it is working in the meaning except for a reason. He said: The reason is that it is a narration, so if it occurs in something that it does not work on, then it is a narration or a wish, but if it works, then it remains as it is.
41:49: And His statement: Man does not tire of supplicating for good means that the Most High says: The disbeliever in God does not tire of supplicating for good, meaning that he supplicates for good and asks his Lord for it. Good in this context means money and physical health. He says: He does not tire of asking for that. And if evil touches him means: If harm befalls him in his soul, such as illness or difficulty in his livelihood or withholding of his provision. And he despairs of hopelessness means: He is hopeless of God's mercy and of His removing the evil that has befallen him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, A person does not tire of praying for good, he says: the unbeliever. And if evil touches him, he despairs of hopelessness, despairing of goodness. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Man does not get tired, he said: He does not get bored. And he mentioned that in Abdullah’s reading, it is: Man does not get tired of supplication for good.
41:50: God Almighty says: And if We remove from this disbeliever what has befallen him of illness in his soul and harm, and hardship in his livelihood and effort, as a mercy from Us, and grant him well-being in his soul after the illness, and provide him with wealth, and expand his livelihood after the effort and harm, he will surely say, ‘This is for me’ before God, because God is pleased with me because He is pleased with my work and what I am continuing upon. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, He will say, ‘This is for me,’ meaning, by my deeds, and I am entitled to this. And I do not think the Hour will occur, meaning, I do not think the Resurrection will occur on the Day it occurs. And if I am returned to my Lord, meaning, if the Resurrection also occurs, and I am returned to God alive after my death, I will have with Him the best, meaning, I will have wealth and riches with Him. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding His statement: Indeed, I have with Him the best, meaning: wealth. Then We will surely inform those who disbelieve of what they did, meaning, the Most High says: “Then We will surely inform these disbelievers about God, who wish falsehoods from Him, on the Day when they return to Him, of what they did of sins and evil deeds they committed in this world, and then We will recompense them all for that with their recompense. “And We will surely make them taste of a severe punishment,” and that severe punishment is their eternity in the fire of Hell, where they neither die nor live.
41:51: God Almighty says: And when We bestow favor upon the disbeliever, and remove his affliction, and provide him with wealth and abundance, and bestow upon him good health and well-being, he turns away from what We have called him to do in terms of obeying Him, and turns away from it. And distances himself means: And distances himself from responding to Our call to what We have called him to do. And by his side he means his direction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned that he said that: Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement: He turned away and moved away from his side, he says: He turned away: he turned his face away, and moved away from his side, he says: he distanced himself. His saying: And if evil touches him, he is a man of abundant supplication. By abundant, he means: a lot. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, The one who has a long supplication means: a lot, and that is what people say: So-and-so prolonged the supplication: if he increased it, and likewise he prolonged his supplication.
41:52: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “Say, O Muhammad, to those who deny what you have brought them from your Lord of this Qur’an: ‘Have you considered, O people, if this which you deny is from God and then you disbelieved in it? Are you not separated from the truth and far from what is right?’ So He replaced the separation with the report, saying: ‘Who is more astray than he who is in extreme dissension?’” since its meaning was understood. And His statement: Who is more astray than he who is in extreme dissension? means: Tell them who is more astray from the straight path and takes a path other than the right one, than he who is in separation from the command of God and fears Him, far from guidance.
41:53: God Almighty says: We will show these deniers of the message We sent down to Muhammad, Our servant, Our signs in the horizons. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the signs that God promised to show these people. Some of them said: What is meant by the signs in the horizons are the events that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, experienced in the regions and outskirts of the land of the polytheists of Mecca. And by His saying: and in their souls, it means the conquest of Mecca. Who said that? Abu Kurayb told us: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Amr ibn Abi Qais, on the authority of Al-Munhal, regarding his statement: We will show them Our signs in the horizons, he said: The appearance of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, over the people. Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, We will show them Our signs in the horizons, meaning: what horizons We will open for you, O Muhammad. And within themselves, in the people of Mecca, meaning: We will open Mecca for you. Others said: What he meant by that is that he will show them the stars of the night and its moon, and the sun of the day, and that is what he promised them that he would show them in the horizons. They said: What he meant by the horizons is the horizons of the sky, and by his saying, and in their souls, is the path of defecation and urination. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves, he said: The horizons of the heavens: their stars, sun, and moon that move, and signs within themselves as well. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the first opinion, which is what Al-Suddi said. That is because God, the Almighty, promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would show these polytheists who denied Him signs in the horizons. It is not reasonable that He would threaten them by showing them what they saw. Rather, it must be a promise from Him to them that He would show them what they had not seen before, namely the appearance of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the outskirts of their country and in their country. As for the stars, the sun, and the moon, they saw them often before and after, and there is no reason to threaten them that He would show them that. And His saying: Until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth, God Almighty says: I show these polytheists Our events with their limbs and through them so that they may know the truth of what We sent down to Muhammad and what We revealed to him of the promise to him that We will make manifest what We sent him with of the religion over all religions, even if the polytheists hate it. And His statement: Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness? God Almighty says: Is it not sufficient for your Lord, O Muhammad, that He is a Witness over everything that His creation does? Nothing of it escapes His knowledge, and He will reward them for their deeds, the doer of good for good, and the doer of evil will receive his reward. As for his saying: that there are two aspects: One of them is that it is in the accusative case by way of repeating the ba, so the meaning of the statement then is: Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is a witness over all things? The other is that it is in the nominative case, nominative by his saying: is sufficient, so the meaning of the statement is: Is it not sufficient for your Lord that He is a witness over all things?
41:54: God Almighty says: Indeed, these deniers of God’s signs are in doubt about meeting their Lord, meaning that they are in doubt about resurrection after death and their return to their Lord. As Muhammad told us, he said: Ahmad told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. He said: In doubt. And His statement: Indeed, He encompasses all things. God Almighty says: Indeed, God encompasses all of what He created with knowledge of all of it and power over it. Nothing of it that He willed escapes Him, but He who has power over it is the One who knows its place.
